title: Go SDK: Resilient streaming responses with context-aware cancellation and deadline propagation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Add a robust streaming implementation to the Go SDK that cleanly integrates with context.Context for cancellation and deadline propagation, supports configurable retry/backoff semantics for transient stream failures, and offers ergonomic hooks for consumers to manage partial results and backpressure. This ticket covers API design, runtime implementation, tests, docs and a small example app that demonstrates graceful cancellation, deadline inheritance, and retry behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Go SDK exposes a Stream() API that accepts context.Context and returns a typed stream iterator with Next()/Recv()/Close() semantics
Cancelling the context immediately aborts reads and releases underlying network/kvm resources; callers receive a defined error (context.Canceled or context.DeadlineExceeded)
Server-initiated and network transient errors trigger configurable retries up to N attempts with jittered backoff without duplicating already-delivered tokens
A unit/integration test matrix covers: normal streaming, client-side cancellation, deadline expiry, mid-stream server disconnects, retry succeeded, retry exhausted
Documentation page and Go example (examples/stream-cancel) demonstrate recommended patterns and show expected error types
Benchmark demonstrates no more than 5% tail-latency regression for single-stream latency compared to baseline non-retrying impl under p95 workload
No resource leaks in long-running streaming acceptance tests (validated by heap/conn counts and CI stress tests)
SDK API is backward compatible for existing users using the older raw streaming endpoint (compat shim included)
PRs approved by two engineers and one PM, and merged to main with passing CI and integration tests against staging runtime
Release notes and migration snippet included in console and docs PR
specification: API: Add Client.Stream(ctx context.Context, req StreamRequest, opts ...StreamOption) (StreamReader, error). StreamReader exposes Recv() (StreamEvent, error) and Close() error plus Context() context.Context to let callers derive child contexts. Behavior: Recv blocks until next token/event or context cancellation. When the provided ctx is canceled or its deadline exceeded, Recv returns a wrapped error that canonicalizes to context.Canceled or context.DeadlineExceeded. Retries: transient transport errors (network timeouts, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF, grpc Unavailable, HTTP 5xx) will trigger at-most N retries with exponential backoff and full/partial resume semantics where the SDK attempts to resume the stream using last-acknowledged sequence ID when supported by server. Options: WithRetryPolicy(retryCount,int, baseDelay time.Duration, maxDelay time.Duration, jitter bool), WithStreamBuffer(maxPendingTokens int), WithResumeOnReconnect(bool). Backpressure: the SDK enforces an internal token queue that bound memory; users can supply WithStreamBuffer to tune the queue. Compatibility: existing streaming helper functions are retained and delegated to the new implementation via a compat wrapper.
implementation_notes: Add new types in github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/stream: StreamRequest, StreamOption, StreamReader, StreamEvent
Implement transport layer in transport/http_stream.go to translate HTTP chunked streaming to StreamEvent with sequence IDs
Implement retry coordinator that can serialize resume token and replay non-duplicated segments where server supports resume; server resume protocol is documented in internal/design/stream-resume.md
Hook context cancellation into underlying http.Request with req = req.WithContext(ctx) and ensure all goroutines select on ctx.Done() where appropriate
Add compatibility shim in examples for older code paths (examples/legacy_stream_adapter.go)
Add unit tests for Recv cancellation behavior by using a net.Pipe() fake transport to control timing
Add integration tests using staging-runtime that intentionally kills connections mid-stream and asserts retry/resume behavior
Add benchmarks under sdk/bench/stream_bench_test.go comparing baseline vs new impl
Update CHANGELOG and docs/sdks/go/streaming.md and add examples/stream-cancel/main.go
decisions: Use context.Context as the single source of truth for cancellation/deadlines rather than adding separate CloseWithTimeout APIs to avoid API surface bloat
Implement retries only for transport-level transient errors; application-level error frames from the model will not be retried automatically
Expose a StreamReader.Context() so callers can derive child contexts with per-call deadlines without losing original cancellation semantics
Opted to make resume behavior opt-in (WithResumeOnReconnect) because not all backends currently provide robust resume tokens
Do not automatically duplicate application-level events on retry; instead SDK will resume from last-acknowledged sequence ID to avoid duplication
tradeoffs: Pros: tight context integration feels idiomatic to Go callers and simplifies cancellation reasoning
Cons: callers need to be aware of deadline propagation; a mistakenly short deadline will abort streams early
Pros: opt-in resume avoids surprising semantics for customers on backends that don't support resume
Cons: implementing resume increases complexity in transport and testing matrix
Decision to only retry transport errors keeps application correctness but leaves responsibility for higher-level idempotency to caller
testing_plan: Unit tests: cancellation path, deadline propagation, Recv error semantics, buffer bounds
Integration tests: staging runtime tests that kill connections, validate resume on reconnect when enabled
Stress tests: long-running multi-stream test (1000 concurrent streams for 10m) to detect leaks
Fuzz tests: malformed chunk boundaries and truncated events to validate error handling
Benchmarks: p50/p95/p99 latency comparisons and throughput with different buffer sizes
CI gating: require integration tests with staging runtime to pass before merging to main
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag STREAM_V2_ENABLED. Stage rollout: enable for internal dev accounts, then beta customers, then full by default in next minor release. Monitor metrics: stream failure rate, retry rate, duplicate-token incidents, connection leak counts, and client-side error types (context canceled vs other). Have quick rollback by toggling STREAM_V2_ENABLED in client config and providing compat-wrapper fallback.
notes: Early integration runs show cancellation behaves as expected but discovered a goroutine leak when Recv returns an error without Close being called — added additional guard to ensure transport cleanup on first Recv error. Follow-up task may be created to add finalizer-based leak detector in CI.
